newsitem.title: UK: Morgan Stanley talking to Barclays on custody.
newsitem.headline: Morgan Stanley talking to Barclays on custody.

text.p: U.S. investment bank Morgan Stanley said on Sunday it was in talks with Britain's Barclays Bank over possible future cooperation in the field of global custody.

"Due to their extensive customer/provider inter-relationships in global custody, Barclays and Morgan Stanley are in discussions to explore the potential for future cooperation in that area," Morgan Stanley said in a statement.
"A further announcement will be made at a later date," it added.
Britain's Sunday Telegraph had earlier reported that Barclays was in negotiations to sell its global custody business to Morgan Stanley.
The report said that an announcement of a deal was expected shortly. It said Barclay's global custody business handles funds worth about 200 billion stg.

Barclays had earlier declined comment on the report, saying it never responded to speculation. Representatives of the two companies could not be contacted late on Sunday night to add anything to Morgan Stanley's three-line statement.
However, banking sources said that any agreement between the two was likely to result in Morgan Stanley acquiring Barclay's global custody business, as the newspaper report had suggested.

The Sunday Telegraph said Barclays chief executive Martin Taylor had decied that custody was not a core business because of its wafer-thin margins, high compliance costs and hunger for technology spending.

Once consisting of little more than the safe keeping of shares and bonds, global custody has expanded to cover a range of services from investment accounting to performance measurement and securities lending.
The business is rapidly consolidating and any deal would make Morgan Stanley one of the world's leading custodians.
